clocks.label: SCO BISHKEK
clocks.why: Putin, Xi and Modi meet for the bloc's 25th-anniversary summit. It prices the Russia-China file: whether Moscow's deepening dependence buys Beijing anything nameable, or whether the communique is again a photograph of a partnership that agrees on nothing operational.

clocks.label: G20 ASHEVILLE
clocks.why: Bessent hosts G20 finance ministers on US soil after skipping the South Africa process, demanding members sever business ties with Iran. This clock prices GEO-010 and GEO-011: whether the sanctions siege gets multilateral cover or stays a unilateral instrument other governments quietly route around.

clocks.label: XI SUMMIT
clocks.why: The state visit that GEO-006 (85%) and GEO-012 (31%) both hang on. If a Hormuz concession appears only in the thirty days AFTER it, the leverage-play read is confirmed; if it appears before, the read is wrong.

clocks.label: RU FUEL EXPORT BAN
clocks.why: Moscow's ban on most diesel, gasoline and jet exports, first imposed July 8 and now weighed for a second extension. Each extension is a public admission of how much refining Ukraine's drones have taken offline - and it removes product from a world market where Hormuz is still restricted.

clocks.label: IRAN-OMAN WINDOW
clocks.why: The 30-60 day technical-talks clock from the Muscat corridor framework. If it lapses with no verified minesweeping calendar and no corridor coordinates, the sixth near-breakthrough-then-condition cycle completes and the nobody-is-hurrying read on Hormuz strengthens.

clocks.label: US MIDTERMS
clocks.why: The master clock every captured file is priced against. Pump prices, casualties and endless-war branding all bill on this date - it is why not-in-a-hurry is the posture, and why a visible retreat before it is the falsifier on the coalition-capture hypothesis.

quiz.q: Russia's defence ministry says its planned strikes on Ukraine's grid are retaliation for Kyiv's drone campaign. What has that Ukrainian campaign actually done to Russia?
options: Cut Russian crude production to its lowest level since the Soviet collapse
Pushed Russian refinery runs to a 24-year low and forced a ban on most fuel exports
Destroyed the pipelines carrying Russian crude to China
Halted Russian oil revenue almost entirely
quiz.why: The target is refining, not production. Russian refinery runs fell to roughly 3.6m barrels a day in July, the lowest since May 2002, and Moscow banned most diesel, gasoline and jet exports from July 8 to keep its own pumps supplied. Crude keeps flowing; the ability to turn it into fuel is what is being taken away.

quiz.q: Treasury moved against Banque Misr's UAE branches rather than a Chinese state bank. What does that choice suggest about the sanctions strategy?
options: Chinese banks have no exposure to Iranian oil trade
Egypt is a larger conduit for Iranian oil than China is
The expensive target is being deliberately spared while the instrument is demonstrated on a cheap one
The Treasury lacks legal authority over Chinese institutions
quiz.why: Banque Misr sits in a G20 member with little capacity to retaliate; China is the buyer that would actually decide the outcome and has been left untouched. An enforcer that repeatedly picks the cheapest available nail is telling you which nail it does not intend to hit - which is why the forecast on a Chinese bank designation went down, not up.

quiz.q: Why does the brief treat Mojtaba Khamenei's WRITTEN Islamic Unity Week message as meaningful evidence rather than routine?
options: Written messages are forbidden for a Supreme Leader on religious occasions
The occasion is the one his father delivered live for over three decades, so the medium was a conspicuous choice
It contained a new threat against the Gulf states
It was the first communication from him in six months
quiz.why: The information is in the missed focal occasion. If the Leader is a legitimacy token the IRGC holds rather than an operating ruler, handlers avoid live exposure exactly when it is most expected - so a text post at the highest-salience clerical moment of the year carries more signal than another quiet day would.

quiz.q: What makes the Pacific Islands Forum in Palau a useful gauge for China policy, despite its small size?
options: Its members control a chokepoint for global shipping
It is where diplomatic recognition is bought and sold one small state at a time, and where pressure that pauses can be told apart from pressure that ratchets
It has the authority to admit Taiwan to the United Nations
Its decisions bind Chinese fishing fleets
quiz.why: Recognition is retail in the Pacific: a switch costs one small state's decision and buys lasting maritime and diplomatic geometry. It is also a low-cost test of the harvest-cover hypothesis - whether Beijing's current softness is a pause bought for the September summit or a ratchet that keeps turning through it.

quiz.q: A headline reads: US declares the Strait of Hormuz cleared of Iranian mines. Which single observable would best tell you whether the strait has actually reopened?
options: A CENTCOM commander repeating the declaration on video
Published war-risk insurance premia falling back under 3% of hull value
Iran issuing a statement welcoming international shipping
Brent crude falling below $85
quiz.why: Underwriters, not commanders or ministries, price the reopening - they are paying real money on their own read of the risk and have no incentive to flatter anyone. The IMO secretary-general disputed the mine-free claim and the JMIC kept its severe rating, so the declaration and the insurance market disagree; the premium is the one that settles bets.

decode.claim: The United States has entered the biggest oil deal in history, taking majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil, more than doubling American oil reserves, substantially lowering gas prices, and at no cost to the American taxpayer.
decode.source: Trump social-media post, Aug 28; structure briefed by a US official
decode.verdictNote: Framing, and the load-bearing distinction is where reserves are counted. Oil reserves are booked to the ground they sit in, not to the nationality of the shareholder — 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan proven reserves stay Venezuelan reserves under every accounting convention, and what Washington describes buying is 55% of a new company's effective output, split between an equity stake and the right to buy barrels at cost. That is a claim on production, not title. “No cost to the American taxpayer” is also narrower than it sounds: it means no appropriated cash this year, not no sovereign risk on a 100-year concession under an interim government installed after the US removed its predecessor.
decode.reality: Trump announced the deal on social media on Aug 28 and named Marco Rubio, Pete Hegseth and Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodríguez as the negotiators. A US official describes a joint venture with a private Venezuelan company covering 17 fields, a 100-year lease over 65 billion barrels of proven reserves, and a 55% US share of effective output split between ownership and at-cost purchase rights, with at-cost barrels going to the Strategic Petroleum Reserve and the military. Venezuela is currently producing about 1.23m barrels a day — its highest since February 2019 — of which Chevron's joint venture accounts for roughly 260,000. For scale on the reserves claim: US proved crude and lease-condensate reserves were 46.4bn barrels at end-2023 (EIA), so 65bn is indeed the larger number, which is exactly why adding it across a border is the move worth catching.
decode.aspiration: No agreement text has been published. The private operator has not been officially named (reporting points to Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt). Nobody has said how the 55% divides between equity and at-cost rights, who funds the roughly $100bn of investment Rubio cited, or which sanctions authorisation lets a US government entity hold the stake. Venezuela's constitution treats hydrocarbons as inalienable public domain and no National Assembly ratification has been shown. Chevron and ExxonMobil both declined to comment — no major has committed capital. On prices: energy analysts Amy Myers Jaffe and Kevin Book both say the infrastructure work takes years and billions, and will not move the pump price this weekend.

angles.effect: Gains an energy-price story and a below-market SPR refill before the midterms, bought with an announcement rather than an appropriation — the cheapest possible instrument, and the reason it arrived as a post rather than a treaty.
Converts a transitional mandate into a governing one: recognition, sanctions relief and a promised $100bn of capital, paid for by pre-committing decades of the country's principal asset.

The concession runs through a private company, so operatorship of what a US official called the world's second-largest private oil company by reserves lands with one businessman rather than a state entity — while Chevron and Exxon pay nothing and say nothing, which is the correct position while the legal text, the sanctions carve-out and the arbitration clause are all missing.

angles.party: Venezuelans and any future elected government
angles.effect: Carry the bill. They inherit a contract they did not vote on, and a dilemma: honour it and a century of the resource is spoken for; break it and sanctions and the security question come straight back.

The party absent from the announcement. If Venezuelan heavy sour genuinely reaches Gulf refiners in volume, the Canadian heavy discount widens — Alberta pays part of the price of a Washington announcement and gets no seat in it.

clock.d90: Sentiment, not molecules. Production stays near 1.2–1.3m b/d and there is no measurable pump-price effect. The testable event is the signing session Caracas says is scheduled for next week, and whether a document appears with it.
clock.m18: The capital question resolves. Either an OFAC authorisation and a published contract exist and a major commits real money, or the deal stays a press release with a lease number attached. Watch whether output moves toward the stated 1.5m b/d.
clock.y7: Where 65bn either becomes barrels or does not. Orinoco extra-heavy crude needs upgraders, diluent, power and port capacity that do not exist at the claimed scale today — and this is also where political durability is tested, when a Venezuelan government that did not sign this has to decide whether to honour it.

watch: The published contract text — its governing law and arbitration seat, the legal name of the joint venture and the identity of the private operator. Its absence is currently the single biggest hole in the claim.
An OFAC general licence or amended sanctions authorisation covering the venture — without one, no US major can lawfully fund it.
A Venezuelan National Assembly ratification vote or gazette publication, given the constitution's inalienable-public-domain clause.
A first at-cost cargo delivered into the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, with a dated bill of lading and the price paid versus market.
Venezuelan monthly production in OPEC secondary-source figures crossing 1.5m b/d.
decode.easy: The president said America now controls 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's oil, that it costs you nothing and that it will lower fuel prices. No signed contract has been published, the oil stays in Venezuelan ground under Venezuelan law, and getting it out takes years — so today this mostly helps the government in Caracas that needs the money and the private company that gets to run the fields.

decode.claim: Venezuela preserves ownership of and sovereignty over its resources under a 25-year agreement that returns $19 from every barrel sold to the US, worth up to $209 billion.
decode.source: Delcy Rodríguez, Venezuela's acting president, televised address
decode.verdictNote: Partly true, and the half that survives matters: Venezuela does keep legal title, because what Washington describes acquiring is a stake in a company plus purchase rights, not ownership of rock. Both governments can be telling the truth about that at the same time. What they cannot both be right about is the term — Caracas says 25 years, Washington says a 100-year lease — and the money does not reconcile either: 1.5m barrels a day at $19 a barrel is roughly $10bn a year, so $209bn is only reachable as a multi-decade cumulative total, not an annual one.
decode.reality: Rodríguez said in a televised address that the deal covers 17 strategic oilfields with an initial production target of 1.5m barrels a day plus eight greenfield blocks, that $19 from every barrel sold to the US flows to Caracas, and that Venezuela retains “ownership of and sovereignty” over its natural resources “while leveraging capital, technology and operational expertise.” She said agreements would be signed the following week. Venezuela's actual output today is about 1.23m b/d, with a government target of 1.37m by year-end — so 1.5m is an increase, not a transformation.
decode.aspiration: The 25-year term is asserted, not documented, and is directly contradicted by the US description of a 100-year lease. The $209bn figure, the $100bn of inbound investment, the eight greenfield blocks and the signing itself are all forward-looking. No text has been published, no National Assembly ratification has been reported, and the constitutional question — whether an inalienable public-domain resource can be committed this way at all — is untouched in her address.

angles.effect: Turns an interim mandate into a sovereignty-preserving national win and gets a fiscal number, $19 a barrel, that she can put in a budget speech. The word 'sovereignty' is doing the political work the term sheet cannot.

angles.party: The PSUV base and the Chavista tradition
angles.effect: Asked to accept foreign operatorship of the industry Chávez nationalised. 'Ownership retained' is the formula that makes that survivable inside the party — which is precisely why it was the first phrase in the address.
Boxed in. Opposing the deal means opposing sanctions relief and $100bn of investment; supporting it means blessing terms negotiated by a government seated after a US operation removed the last one.
Gains by conceding the word. Control of output was always the object, so letting Caracas keep the language of sovereignty costs nothing and stabilises the counterpart it needs to sign.

angles.party: Venezuelan citizens and every government after this one
angles.effect: Pay the spread. They receive $19 a barrel while the venture keeps the rest of the value chain, and they carry the difference between a 25-year commitment and a 100-year one — a gap of three generations that nobody has put in writing, agreed to by an unelected acting president on television.

clock.d90: The signing session Caracas promised. The only thing that matters is whether a stated term appears in a document — 25 or 100 — and whether the National Assembly touches it.
clock.m18: Whether $19-a-barrel receipts actually appear in Venezuelan fiscal accounts, and whether output moves from 1.23m toward the stated 1.5m b/d.
clock.y7: Whether the term survives a change of government in Caracas or of administration in Washington. A concession is paper until an institution enforces it.

watch: The stated term in the signed text — the one number that settles the 25-versus-100-year contradiction between the two announcing governments.
Whether the $19 per barrel is structured as royalty, tax or profit share, and whether it is indexed to price.
A National Assembly ratification vote or publication in the Gaceta Oficial.
A Venezuelan budget line showing receipts from the venture, in the next fiscal presentation.
Whether the eight greenfield blocks appear in the same instrument as the 17 producing fields or in a separate, later one.
decode.easy: Venezuela's acting president said the country keeps ownership of its oil, that the deal lasts 25 years and pays Venezuela $19 a barrel. The ownership part is fair — but Washington described the same deal as a 100-year lease, and the $209 billion she cited only works as a total over decades, not per year.

decode.claim: The violence in the West Bank villages of Qusra and Jalud was criminal, committed by a handful of rioters who are violating the law and harming Israel's standing in the world.
decode.verdictNote: The condemnation is real and unusually direct from this prime minister — but the load-bearing word is “handful,” which recasts a documented and recurring pattern as isolated deviance. The follow-through so far is evidentiary rather than prosecutorial: the military impounded vehicles for a police file, and no arrests were announced. Yesh Din's monitoring of 1,701 police investigations since 2005 finds 93.8% closed with no indictment and only 3% ending in conviction, so a statement and a case file are not the same object.
decode.reality: Dozens of settlers descended on Qusra on Saturday after nearly three weeks of tension, throwing stones at residents and barricading themselves inside a house with Palestinians still in it; in nearby Jalud settlers attacked a Palestinian family and an NBC News crew. The army removed settlers from the Palestinian home, separated the groups, and confiscated vehicles suspected of having been used to reach the area as evidence for a police investigation. Netanyahu's statement was issued the same day and is a rare rebuke.
decode.aspiration: Everything downstream of the words. No arrests were announced, no suspects named, no indictments filed, no administrative orders issued against Israeli citizens for these incidents. Nothing in the statement names an instrument — no policing change, no deadline, no minister tasked. Whether the impounded vehicles produce identified suspects is the open question, and the base rate says most such files close as “offender unknown”.

angles.effect: Buys international cover at zero coalition cost. Words carry no price with his partners; and note the injury he names is to 'the law-abiding Jewish community' and to 'Israel's standing in the world' — the framing is reputational, not about the people who were attacked.
Lose nothing. The statement stops precisely where a coalition fight would begin: it names no policy, no ministry and no enforcement target, so the national-security portfolio is untouched.

Handed an expectation without new authority or a deadline. The statement even describes the army as being 'interfered with' — casting the force responsible for order in the territory as the aggrieved party rather than the accountable one.

angles.party: Residents of Qusra and Jalud, and the reporters covering them
angles.effect: Pay in full and in advance. They face recurring attacks and a 93.8% no-indictment rate, which is the number that actually predicts their next year — not the sentence read out in Jerusalem. An NBC crew was attacked alongside them, and unpunished attacks on journalists mean fewer journalists in those villages, which erodes the evidence base condemnations depend on.

angles.party: European and US officials weighing settler sanctions
angles.effect: Handed the counter-argument. A prime-ministerial condemnation is the strongest available case for holding off on designations — which is a benefit to Israel's government whether or not a single indictment follows.

clock.d90: Whether the Qusra and Jalud files produce named suspects and indictments, or close. This is the only window in which the statement can be falsified cheaply.
clock.m18: Whether the 2026 indictment and conviction rates move off their twenty-year band. One prosecution is an anecdote; a shift in the percentage is a policy change.
clock.y7: Whether any enforcement architecture in Area C changes at all — jurisdiction, police staffing, or the standing of Israeli civilians under military versus civil law.

watch: A named indictment with a case number arising from the Qusra or Jalud incidents.
Whether the impounded vehicles yield identified suspects, or the files close on “offender unknown” — the disposition of those specific vehicles is the cheapest available test.
Any administrative detention or restraining order issued against Israeli citizens for these attacks.
Yesh Din's next data sheet and the 2026 closure and conviction percentages.
Whether the national security ministry publicly backs, contradicts or slow-walks the police investigation.
decode.easy: Israel's prime minister called the settler attacks on two Palestinian villages criminal, which he rarely does. But so far the army has only impounded some cars and nobody has been arrested — and over twenty years, 94 out of every 100 of these police files have closed with no charges at all.

decode.claim: The prompt reaction of Niger's defence and security forces contained the mutiny and gradually regained control of the sites attacked in Niamey.
decode.source: Niger junta statement read on state television
decode.verdictNote: Partly true — and the tell is inside the wording. A government that held its capital does not need to announce that it “gradually regained control” of sensitive sites; the sentence concedes the sites were lost before it claims they were recovered. Containment itself looks real — the state broadcaster came back on air, and the presidential guard repelled an attempt on the palace — but a diplomatic source told AFP the guard retook the air base “with the help of the Russians,” which, if confirmed, means the regime's own forces were not sufficient. That is the part of the day that has consequences, and it is not in the statement.
decode.reality: Sustained gunfire and explosions were reported on Aug 29 around Base 101, the presidential palace and the state broadcaster in Niamey. Soldiers from the Base 101 barracks opened fire on several sensitive sites after attempting to detain fellow soldiers. Télé Sahel went off air for about an hour before being restored around 10:00. Security sources confirmed an attempted breach of the presidential palace was pushed back by the presidential guard. This is the latest challenge to Abdourahamane Tiani, who took power in the 2023 coup.
decode.aspiration: Almost every operational detail. No casualty figures, no confirmed arrests, no confirmation of airport status, no named plotters, and — the absence that matters most — no dated public appearance by Tiani himself. The Russian assistance rests on a single anonymous diplomatic source and has not been confirmed or denied by Niamey or Moscow. “Contained” is a claim about a moving situation made by the party with the strongest interest in it being over.

angles.effect: Survive the day and acquire a licence for a purge of the officer corps — the standard post-mutiny move, and the one that tells you how frightened they actually were. Watch the arrest list, not the statement.

angles.party: The mutineers, reported as junior officers
angles.effect: If they are named and tried publicly, the regime is confident. If the files stay sealed and the men disappear into detention, it is not — secrecy after a failed coup usually indicates the plot reached higher than the government wants known.

angles.party: Russia and its Africa Corps presence
angles.effect: If the air base really was retaken with Russian help, Moscow converts a security service into standing political leverage over Niamey — over uranium contracts, over basing, over what Niger can refuse later. Protection is the most expensive thing a weak government can accept, and France and the US, already expelled from their Niger bases, have no instrument left to compete for it.

angles.party: The Sahel alliance partners, Mali and Burkina Faso
angles.effect: A wobble in Niamey wobbles all three. Their juntas rest on the same arithmetic of junior officers with weapons and grievances, and each attempt raises the perceived odds for the next — as it does for the uranium buyers repricing supply risk who were consulted by nobody.

Pay in curfews, communications cuts and a security establishment that now has to watch itself as well as the jihadist insurgency in Tillabéri — attention diverted from the threat that actually kills them.

clock.d90: Arrests, a military tribunal, and a reshuffle of the general staff or the presidential guard command. Also whether Tiani appears in person, on a dated broadcast — the cheapest proof of control there is.
clock.m18: Whether the purge stabilises the army or seeds the next attempt, and whether any Russian role formalises into a written basing or training agreement.
clock.y7: The base rate governs. Niger has now seen repeated coups and attempts; a regime that survives by purging its officer corps tends to meet the same event again, and each round narrows the pool of officers it can trust.

watch: A published list of arrested officers and the convening of a military tribunal — names and ranks, not a numbered total.
Tiani appearing in person on state television, with a verifiable date.
An official Nigerien or Russian statement confirming or denying Russian participation at Base 101 — the single missing document that would change the read of the whole day.
Reopening of Diori Hamani international airport and a return to published flight schedules.
Changes to the command of the presidential guard or the army general staff in the next gazette.
decode.easy: Soldiers attacked the presidential palace and an air base in Niger's capital, and the government says it contained the mutiny and took the sites back. Saying you “gradually regained control” admits you lost them first — and a diplomatic source says Russian forces helped, which would mean the government now owes Moscow for its own survival.

track.note: Nothing has resolved yet, and we publish that rather than dress it up. All 22 forecasts were checked against their deadlines in the Aug 30 audit and against early resolution - the Brent band is the only one that can resolve early, on a single daily close outside 80-100, and Brent settled 88.29 mid-band. The first real score lands Sep 24, then the Xi summit and the Chinese-bank question on Oct 1. Every score appears here as it happens, the misses first. A track record you can only see after it looks good is not a track record.

plumbing.read: The buffer is gone and the pressure is now in two places at once. ON RRP sits at $0.17B, down 84% on the month - the reverse-repo parking lot that would absorb any drain of short-end support is effectively empty - while the Fed balance sheet quietly expanded 0.8% to $6.73T. On the physical side, the product market is tightening from both ends: Russian refinery runs at a 24-year low with a fuel export ban running past Sept 1, and Hormuz still moving roughly a tenth of its pre-war traffic. What is still NOT printing is the milkshake tape - oil AND dollar expensive together. The broad dollar is soft at 118.1, down 2.4% on the month, and that remains the strongest live evidence against escalation. Pressure in the plumbing, not yet in the price.
plumbing.epoch: E6 still open — the Sept-2019 repo confession never closed — running alongside E7, the weaponized-settlement rail opened by the 2022 reserve freeze that the record official gold bid is a late chapter of.

series.note: the short end the Fed is buying

easy.bottomLine: Two big fights got louder today without either one crossing a line. Russia says it is about to start bombing Ukraine's electricity system, because Ukraine has spent the summer blowing up the factories that turn Russian oil into fuel. And America's top money official is about to sit down with the world's other finance chiefs and ask them all to cut off Iran - four days after he cut an Egyptian bank out of the dollar for helping Iran move money.
easy.risk: Held at the same level. Nothing new exploded that forces anyone's hand this week: the Gulf is unchanged, no tanker was attacked for a third day, and China and America are both still planning to hold their summit next month. What changed is that two long fights each got a new front - Russia and Ukraine are now openly aiming at each other's energy systems heading into winter, and the fight over Iran moved from ships and cargo to banks.
easy.markets: The number to watch is not the oil price, it is diesel. Russia makes a lot of the world's diesel and can currently make much less of it, so it has stopped exporting most fuel to keep its own gas stations full. At the same time the Strait of Hormuz is still only moving about a tenth of its normal traffic. Less fuel from two places at once is how a war far away shows up at a pump near you.
brief: Russia says it is preparing big attacks on Ukraine's power grid, as payback for Ukraine using drones to wreck Russian oil refineries all summer. It comes right after a Russian strike on an ammunition store near Kyiv killed 38 people, the deadliest single attack this year.

America's Treasury Secretary is hosting the world's finance ministers this week and wants them all to stop doing business with Iran. Days earlier he blocked an Egyptian bank's Dubai branches from the US banking system - but he still has not touched any big Chinese bank, which is the one that would really matter.

Iran's Supreme Leader marked the most important religious week of the year by posting a written message telling Gulf kings to unite against their real enemy. He did not mention the closed strait or the talks - and he did not appear in person, which he has not done for six months.

Taiwan got a seat at a meeting of Pacific island leaders in Palau this week, after being shut out last year. China told the organisers not to allow it, and America publicly said it should - which makes a small summit a good test of how hard China is really pushing right now.

In Guinea-Bissau, the soldiers who seized power last year asked voters to approve a new constitution giving the president much more power. The election that is supposed to end military rule is in December - so they are changing the rules first, then holding the vote.

actors.w: A deal-brander who treats military force as leverage, not doctrine.
actors.g: A visible 'reopened Hormuz, no forever-war' win before the midterms.
actors.m: Called off Iran strikes a fifth time since April, pending a Hormuz deal.
actors.l: Threatens maximally, then delays — the 'decapitation' line is a price tag, not a plan.

actors.w: Career global-macro trader — ex-Soros, broke the Bank of England in 1992.
actors.g: Prove economic warfare can replace kinetic escalation; own the signature policy.
actors.m: Launched 'Economic D-Day' — sanctioning 60 entities across five Iranian lifelines.
actors.l: He is trading Iran's economy like a short position — make every counterparty pre-emptively de-risk.

actors.w: Longtime China/Iran hawk repositioned as the administration's off-ramp diplomat.
actors.g: Land the Hormuz deal that justifies pausing strikes.
actors.m: Told counterparts there will be no new strikes 'for the time being'.
actors.l: The pressure-release valve — when Rubio talks progress, strikes are being deferred.

actors.w: Trump loyalist comfortable as a direct presidential envoy, not a neutral analyst.
actors.g: Deter a Russian move on NATO; recruit Moscow's leverage over Tehran.
actors.m: Made a rare unannounced Moscow trip (Aug 25-27) as the US asked Kyiv to hold long-range strikes.
actors.l: The CIA channel is where the Ukraine and Iran boards secretly connect.

actors.w: Mid-tier cleric who inherited power running his father's office; legitimacy is IRGC-underwritten.
actors.g: Regime and dynastic survival — if he can operationally want anything at all.
actors.m: Unseen for ~6 months; reportedly wounded in the Feb strike; promised footage never delivered.
actors.l: He may be a legitimacy token the IRGC holds in reserve, not a ruler. (Opacity max; exile-sourced.)

actors.w: Career diplomat and JCPOA architect, trusted by securocrats yet fluent with Washington.
actors.g: A face-saving off-ramp that reopens Hormuz without formal capitulation.
actors.m: Kept the negotiation's public face all summer; reportedly admitted he has lost direct contact with Mojtaba.
actors.l: The shock-absorber — his lost-contact admission is the clearest on-record crack in the leadership fiction.

actors.w: Founding Quds Force commander, Interpol-wanted over the 1994 Buenos Aires bombing; a shadow-war operator.
actors.g: IRGC-institutional primacy — keep the Corps' grip on the state and the Hormuz revenue machine.
actors.m: Anchored the August wartime reshuffle that seated a new security committee.
actors.l: With the Leader invisible, Vahidi's IRGC is the actual center of gravity.

actors.w: Elected reformist heart surgeon with a mandate but no coercive power.
actors.g: De-escalation and economic relief; keep the elected government from IRGC eclipse.
actors.m: Signaled the odds of the war widening have decreased; co-signed the August security reshuffle.
actors.l: He governs the economy and the funerals, not the war.

actors.w: The politician who spent a career warning of Iran and finally got a US president to strike it.
actors.g: Political survival and a victory narrative on Iran and Lebanon without rupturing Washington.
actors.m: Squeezed between a war-favoring electorate and US restraint as re-election nears.
actors.l: Read every Iran decision through the 2026 Israeli election calendar.

actors.w: A hawkish Likud loyalist whose authority is political alignment with Netanyahu.
actors.g: Keep maximum military pressure and preserve the option to re-strike Iran.
actors.m: Warned that 'soon we will be required to act again' during the strike lull.
actors.l: The cabinet's designated hawk-voice — the political floor under any ceasefire.

actors.w: KGB officer turned 25-year ruler who sees the war as civilizational, not transactional.
actors.g: Regime survival fused with a maximalist claim — Ukraine out of NATO, recognized gains, a weakened West.
actors.m: Let Peskov declare talks in 'deep pause' while forces press Pokrovsk without an off-ramp.
actors.l: He negotiates only when compelled; battlefield momentum is his diplomacy. A pause is pressure, not fatigue.

actors.w: Long-serving mouthpiece whose words are calibrated Kremlin temperature-setting, not personal position.
actors.g: Nothing of his own — transmit Putin's framing and manage expectations.
actors.m: Voiced the Aug 28 'deep pause, no new proposals' line, rejecting the joint Western plan.
actors.l: Read him as a thermostat, not an actor. A denial is data; a pause is a posture.

actors.w: The most centralized Chinese ruler since Mao; a recent military purge pushed back his Taiwan timetable.
actors.g: National rejuvenation and a stable US truce that buys time to lock in structural advantages.
actors.m: Publicly defiant on Iran sanctions while preserving the Sept 24 summit and the tariff truce.
actors.l: Détente is tactical cover for accumulation — de-escalate where it costs him, harden where it buys leverage.

actors.w: Xi's chief foreign-policy enforcer; when Wang Yi speaks it is not just the FM talking.
actors.g: Land a smooth, deliverable-laden September summit without blowing the truce.
actors.m: Ran summit-prep diplomacy — met the US ambassador Aug 27, urged both sides to overcome obstacles.
actors.l: He carries Xi's authority, so his positive-agenda push is a real signal Beijing wants the summit to hold.

actors.w: Wartime leader managing a domestic corruption shock and total coalition dependence.
actors.g: Sovereignty and guarantees with no legal recognition of lost land — an armistice, not a treaty.
actors.m: Backed the joint Western plan Moscow just 'deep-paused'; kept striking Russian logistics.
actors.l: He must say yes to Washington and no to surrender at once — his room shrinks as Pokrovsk bleeds.

actors.r: Ukraine chief negotiator + spy chief · rising
actors.w: Crimea-born Tatar ex-defense minister trusted by the US envoy channel.
actors.g: A durable, guarantee-backed deal Kyiv can survive politically.
actors.m: Carries the Ukrainian brief through the US-brokered rounds now frozen on Russia's 'deep pause'.
actors.l: Spy chief and negotiator in one loyalist = Zelenskyy centralizing the peace file after the Yermak blow-up.

risk.line: Held at ELEVATED - two theaters each opened a new front today without either crossing an escalation threshold. Russia's defence ministry publicly announced it is preparing massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, explicitly as retaliation for Kyiv's drone campaign that has driven Russian refinery runs to a 24-year low, and it did so the day after a strike on a munitions depot at Myla in Bucha district killed 38 - the deadliest single attack on Ukraine this year. On the Iran file the instrument changed layer rather than intensity: Treasury moved to sever Banque Misr's UAE branches from the US financial system over roughly $1.8bn processed for about 100 companies tied to Iran's shadow-banking network, and Bessent takes the sever-ties demand to the G20 finance table in Asheville on Monday. The Gulf itself was quiet for a third day - no new tanker attack, no Israeli strike inside Iran, and the Supreme Leader's only public act was a written message to Gulf rulers that did not mention the strait. No tripwire fired on any named wire, which is logged deliberately so the non-fire is scoreable.

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover past 50% of pre-war volume
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT, and the biggest move this book has made. Not news - a correction of our own process. PortWatch's latest published day counts THREE transits against its 85/day pre-crisis baseline; Al Jazeera puts mid-July to late-August at about five a day. The strait is running at 4-6% of normal and this needs 50%, a ten- to fifteen-fold rise in 87 days. Suez took roughly a year of clearance AFTER a deal existed, and here there is no deal text at all. We had walked this 55 to 36 in one- and two-point daily steps while the physical gap never moved

forecasts.q: US commits to fixed Venezuelan heavy-crude export infrastructure
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT, cut. States commit to fixed foreign oil-export infrastructure on three-to-seven-year cycles, so a twelve-month window catches announcements and rarely commitments. The evidence agrees: Caracas describes 25 years and 17 fields, Washington describes a 100-year lease, and two governments describing one instrument three generations apart means no instrument exists on paper yet. The motive is untouched - premeditation is what this scores, and concrete is what would show it

forecasts.q: China stands up a third physical-gold venue or a delivery-forcing mechanism
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT, cut - undoing a raise we disowned in the same sentence we made it ('record buying is not evidence of venue construction'). Reference class: China has built two such venues in twenty-four years, Shanghai Gold Exchange in 2002 and its International Board in 2014, which is about 8% in any twelve-month window. The broader delivery-mechanism clause roughly doubles that. 27% required believing the pace is now several times its historical rate

forecasts.q: Brent stays inside the $80-100 band
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT, cut - we replaced a story with arithmetic and the arithmetic disagreed. This had ratcheted up +2, +3, +2, +2 on 'another quiet mid-band day', which is recency weighting wearing a framework's clothes. Done properly from Brent 88.29 with 24 days left: the barriers sit 1.10 and 1.39 standard deviations away at war-regime volatility, giving about 60% survival, plus three or four points because this resolves on daily CLOSES and an intraday spike that closes back inside does not count

forecasts.q: US Hormuz concession within 30 days after the Xi summit
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT, cut - and this is the integrity item. The +6 that lifted this on Aug 28 rested almost entirely on a prediction-market curve. The next day we ruled markets inadmissible for this product. We do not rewrite history, so that entry stands - but leaving a LIVE number standing on evidence we have since disowned would be quietly dishonest, so it was re-derived without it. The thesis survives; the crowd's calendar does not

forecasts.q: Major US/Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT, raised. We were scoring this against the base rate for starting a war between states not already fighting. Wrong class: the US and Israel already ran this campaign once and already resumed it once after a ceasefire collapsed. The right class is recurrence, where breakdown rates for ceasefires with no verifier are far higher. Our own file also holds a dated November trigger - officials describing sanctions as the plan until after the midterms, when a campaign could be back on the table

forecasts.q: Xi state visit to US happens in September
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT, raised. The base rate we ourselves wrote down three weeks ago - announced head-of-state visits with active staff preparation happen about 90% of the time - has been sitting 10 points above our number while every reason for the discount weakened. Sept 24 is on the record, the agenda is being worked, Xi is booked for Bishkek on Sept 1, and no cancellation signal survived the sanctions round

forecasts.q: Hormuz at full pre-war normal
forecasts.note: WEEKLY AUDIT. Same correction at the harder bar, sized smaller because February absorbs more friction. Three to five transits a day to above 110 sustained is a twenty- to thirty-fold move. Flagged honestly: this and the GEO-001 cut run off ONE framework, and it has a dated falsifier - transits above 40 a day for two straight weeks before Oct 15 breaks the argument and sends both back up

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire holds 30+ days
forecasts.note: Held after this morning's cut. The outside view supports it - about 79% of interstate wars end within two years, and Ukraine at 4.5 years is deep in the tail where the odds of stopping get LOWER, not higher. Each of the 2022, 2023 and 2024 winter energy campaigns was followed by no ceasefire in season

forecasts.q: Mojtaba makes a verified live public appearance
forecasts.note: Held after this morning's cut, which was the strongest negative evidence this question has had. He marked Islamic Unity Week - the occasion his father delivered live for over thirty years - with a written Telegram post. Not re-counted here: spending one fact twice is how a book talks itself into a conclusion

forecasts.q: Fed's standing T-bill purchase program still running at end-2026
forecasts.note: Held. The exit got harder, not nearer: the reverse-repo buffer that would absorb a drain is down to $0.17B while the balance sheet expanded to $6.73T. Facilities persist when the conditions that would justify ending them deteriorate

forecasts.q: US sanctions a top-10 Chinese bank before the Xi summit
forecasts.note: Held. Treasury moved on correspondent banking and chose Banque Misr's UAE branches - a G20 member with no retaliation capacity - and touched no Chinese bank. An enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is sparing the expensive one

forecasts.q: Economic D-Day works: China cuts Iranian oil >50%, sustained
forecasts.note: Held. Hufbauer and Pape put sanctions success at 5-35%, and this sits at the low end: great power, core interest, and an enforcer visibly declining to impose the cost that would make the demand bite. Enforcement widened to correspondent banking this week, but the question asks about Beijing

forecasts.q: IF a Hormuz deal happens, it preserves Iranian transit administration
forecasts.note: Held. Ostovar's thesis - the IRGC converts crisis into permanent institution - is operating in real time, and the Muscat technical agenda still explicitly covers the future administration of the strait, not just passage through it

forecasts.q: Russian Q4 territorial gains fall below the Q2-Q3 average
forecasts.note: Held, and the outside view supports it: autumn mud and then winter have historically depressed mechanized tempo against summer, before Kofman's manpower-crossover argument adds anything. Offset by two live axes and the chance Pokrovsk falls as a step change

forecasts.q: Israel-Hezbollah escalates to multi-week campaign
forecasts.note: Held. Fortna's finding is the anchor: ceasefires with an agreed third-party verifier hold materially better, and this framework still has no verifier while the party being disarmed rejects the premise

forecasts.q: China quarantine or blockade of Taiwan
forecasts.note: Held. Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building, not the event. Fravel and Mastro: the command purge pushed the kinetic timetable right

forecasts.q: US-China tariff truce collapses before Nov expiry
forecasts.note: Held. Negotiated truces rarely collapse before their own expiry while both sides are staging a summit inside the window. Still no touch on the tariff schedule, and the bank sanctioned this week was Egyptian

forecasts.q: IF Ukraine fighting stops 30+ days pre-2028: armistice, no peace treaty
forecasts.note: Held. Stalemated interstate wars end in armistices far more often than in signed peace treaties - Korea 1953, Iran-Iraq 1988. If anything this is conservative

forecasts.q: Security-elite fracture in Iran (IRGC defection, coup, mass purge)
forecasts.note: Held. The decapitation-survival literature says security elites usually cohere. Takeyh's test needs a verified defection or purge - an invisible Leader is evidence about who rules, not about cohesion cracking

forecasts.q: Saudi Arabia publicly moves toward enrichment or the bomb
forecasts.note: Held. Overt announcements are rare because hedging is normally covert, so this number structurally undercounts the real trend. Live pathway now named and watched: the Mecca defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye is exactly the vehicle a nuclear-sharing arrangement would surface through

forecasts.q: Bitcoin's cycle top prints at or below ~$150k
forecasts.note: Held. The adoption-saturation model is untouched by this week's flow. Wide bars - Bitcoin has never traded through a real recession

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (NEW — the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Opens at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — 75% → 82%
hypotheses.d: Week's biggest mover, on three strands independent of the Israeli/exile channel. Pezeshkian said on Iranian state TV that communication with Khamenei is 'very difficult' — Tehran's own president, against his own interest. Washington routed its peace offer not to Araghchi but to Mohsen Rezaee, career IRGC commander-in-chief now running the security council. Cipher Brief: 'Tehran isn't saying who is actually in charge.' Capped at 82% because the state has promised footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders — that is the falsifier, and it is coming.

hypotheses.name: Nobody’s hurrying on Hormuz — HELD at 60%
hypotheses.d: The near-breakthrough-then-condition pattern fired a sixth time (Iran–Oman interim corridor and 30–60 days of technical talks, against Ghalibaf restating the full condition stack). Deliberately not moved: it is already priced, and a minesweeping calendar is what an honest process looks like too. The real test is live — the offer sits with the IRGC, so Tehran's answer is the experiment.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — 55% → 60%
hypotheses.d: The discriminating split signal arrived: PLA sorties kept declining while the coast guard escalated in kind — CCG 2307 pressing a Japanese coast guard ship in the strait Aug 6–10, which AEI reads as testing whether foreign vessels will obey PRC authority. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up is the ratchet signature. Capped at +5; the stated tell is what the coast guard does through the Sept 24 visit.

hypotheses.name: NEW · Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it opens at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts, and the reporting frames it in plain words as an alternative to Gulf oil routed through Hormuz. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Operation Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Mundane alternative, named and live: drugs, migration politics, regime-change, with the barrel a bonus. Falsifiers — cut hard if export volumes stay token (the $2-2.8bn tranches are a rounding error against control of 65bn bbl), if Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing does not actually swing off the Middle East, or if the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appears. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz, geography does not work that way — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Real Orinoco or Maracaibo channel-dredging and dedicated heavy-crude terminals WOULD be the premeditation tell. Unconfirmed today; it is the thing to watch.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — 45% → 52%
hypotheses.d: Economic Outcast hit ~60 teapots, tankers and traders and touched no Chinese state major and no bank — Treasury sent the majors a warning letter instead. Maximum pressure on Iran, calibrated to stop exactly short of anything that would detonate the Sept 24 summit. Held to +7 because the Munir offer is a real concession, and $4.10 gas before midterms is real evidence against premeditation.

hypotheses.name: NEW · A pre-announcement leak into oil futures
hypotheses.d: Four times in the war window, nine- and ten-figure short bets landed 15–20 minutes before an Iran announcement: ~$2.2bn across crude, gasoil and gasoline before Trump's Mar 23 pause post; ~$950m before the Apr 7 ceasefire; ~$760m before Iran said Hormuz would open. ~$7bn total; CFTC probing, four members of Congress demanding answers. Split: deliberate leak 45 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 25 / coincidence 10. This is the only entry in the book whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event rather than pattern-matched after — which is why it opens this high. Against it: no episode has surfaced around this week's diplomacy.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 30% → 25%
hypotheses.d: Cut again. The channels that actually moved this week were Oman, Pakistan and the new Mecca defence pact — Russia was absent from every one of them, and still has not offered the mediation this hypothesis expects. Motive 9/10, documentary evidence 0/10, pre-event evidence never. Cut to 15% if nothing surfaces by Sept 30.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Both its live predictions came in favourably this week and it gets credit for neither: the rival leverage hypothesis predicted the same things, and shared predictions are ambience. One more failed pre-summit call and it goes to the epitaph list.

brief.h: Russia says it is preparing mass strikes on Ukraine's grid, and the reason is written on Russia's own refinery map
brief.t: Russia's defence ministry announced on Sunday that it is preparing massive strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, naming as the cause Kyiv's drone campaign against Russian refineries and logistics. It comes a day after a strike on a munitions depot at Myla in the Bucha district near Kyiv killed 38 people with 20 injured and four missing - the deadliest single attack on Ukraine this year, delivered with two Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 130 drones overnight, and the second depot near the capital to blow up in under two months. Strip the podium language and this is no longer a war about territory: it is two states trying to break each other's energy systems on the way into winter. Kyiv's half is measurably working - Russian refinery runs fell to about 3.6 million barrels a day in July, the lowest since May 2002, and Moscow has banned most exports of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel since July 8 to keep its own pumps supplied.
brief.context: Date the rail: this is a late chapter of the epoch in which oil stopped being a commodity and became a war-fighting input, and its nearest ancestor is not 2022 but the Allied oil plan of 1944 - hit refineries rather than front lines, because a refinery is a fixed, costly, slow-to-replace node and an army in the field is none of those things. The desk that decides here is not the Kremlin podium: it is Russia's fuel balance, administered by the energy ministry and the export-ban decree, and on the other side Ukrenergo, which has to hold grid frequency through a heating season. Follow the money and the mechanism: a fuel export ban is a tax on Russian refiners paid to keep Russian drivers quiet, and it withdraws product from a world market where Hormuz is still moving roughly a tenth of its pre-war traffic - which is how a Ukrainian drone becomes a European diesel crack spread and, eventually, a pump price. The base rate is unkind to the strategy Moscow just announced: the US Strategic Bombing Survey found German war production still RISING through 1944 under the heaviest campaign in history, and each of Russia's own 2022, 2023 and 2024 winter energy campaigns was followed by no ceasefire in its season. Framework - Reiter and Wagner: wars end when the two sides' battlefield expectations converge, and opening a new line of effort is divergence, which is why our ceasefire forecast moved down to 15% rather than up. The incompetence alternative deserves naming too: Ukrainian officials are themselves furious that ammunition was stored this close to housing, so part of a 38-death toll is a storage decision, not only a Russian aim point. Falsifier: if six weeks pass with no mass strike on the grid and the Kremlin instead confirms a negotiating round, this was bargaining noise and the downgrade was wrong.

brief.h: Bessent takes the Iran siege to the G20 finance table, four days after cutting an Egyptian bank's Gulf branches out of the dollar
brief.t: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent hosts G20 finance ministers and central bank governors in Asheville, North Carolina on Monday and Tuesday, having shunned the process under South Africa's presidency last year, and his stated agenda is to press other governments to sever business ties with Iran while calming nerves about US debt and bond yields. On Friday, Treasury moved to strip the UAE branches of Banque Misr - Egypt's second-largest bank - of access to US financial institutions, saying they processed roughly $1.8 billion over two years for about 100 companies tied to Iran's shadow-banking network, and separately targeted a Bank Melli Dubai regional manager. That is the campaign migrating from cargo to correspondent banking, the layer where the dollar stops being plumbing and becomes a switch. Note who was chosen: a bank domiciled in a G20 member with no capacity to retaliate, while no Chinese state bank has been touched.
brief.context: Date the rail: this sits on the weaponized-settlement epoch opened in 2022, when freezing a G20 central bank's reserves demonstrated to every reserve manager alive that dollar clearing is a valve someone can close - the same demonstration that explains why central banks bought a record 288.9 tonnes of gold in a quarter when gold was falling. The desk is not the podium: correspondent access is administered by OFAC and FinCEN, and the coercion is actually executed by compliance officers at intermediary banks who de-risk pre-emptively rather than litigate, which is why an announcement bites long before a rule is final. Source discipline, because it changes the object being scored: Treasury is reported as MOVING to revoke access, not as having completed a blocking designation - announced is not binding, and today's effect runs entirely through anticipation. Base rate and framework: Hufbauer's dataset puts sanctions success near a third overall and close to zero against great powers on core interests, while Farrell and Newman's weaponized-interdependence argument warns that a chokepoint decays with use, because every workaround a target builds is permanent. The influence map is unusually legible - principal Washington, agent Treasury, operator the correspondent banks, market the freight and war-risk complex, target Iran - but the party paying this week is Egypt, a debt-stressed food importer, which is exactly what target substitution looks like. Falsifier, and it is the cleanest on the board: a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before the September 24 summit would break the leverage read and send that forecast sharply up instead of down to 7%.

brief.h: Iran's Supreme Leader marked the year's biggest clerical occasion with a written post - and addressed it to Gulf kings, not to Washington
brief.t: Mojtaba Khamenei used Islamic Unity Week, which marks the Prophet's birthday, to publish a message on his Telegram account urging the rulers of Islamic countries, especially in West Asia and the Gulf, to identify your real enemy, understand his plan and confront it, and asking whether rogues without identity would have dared covet Gulf lands had the region been united. Two things about it point in different directions and both matter. Strategically it is a coalition play rather than a negotiation play - aimed at pulling Gulf capitals away from Washington while the strait stays restricted - and it does not mention the Muscat corridor, the joint mine-clearing project or the strait at all. Institutionally it is another written message, at the one occasion in the Iranian calendar his father delivered live as a sermon for more than three decades.
brief.context: Lead with the constraint, not the man: Iran holds a chokepoint it cannot monetize without customers, and its only route out of a naval blockade runs through Gulf neighbours who might be persuaded that the blockade is everyone's problem - so appealing to them is the rational move available to a cornered state, not a mood. Framework - Putnam's two-level game, in which a leader bargains abroad and at home simultaneously: someone preparing a climb-down spends regional capital building cover FOR the deal, while someone spending it on a bloc-against-a-named-enemy frame is buying room to hold the current position, which is why this nudged the Hormuz recovery forecast down a point rather than up. On the second thread the question is which desk actually decides: our working model, at 82%, is that the IRGC rather than the office of the Leader is Iran's operating centre, and the sharpest available test is focal occasions - if the Leader is a legitimacy token held in reserve rather than a ruler, handlers avoid live exposure precisely when it is most expected. The evidentiary weight here is higher than another quiet day because the medium was a conspicuous choice on a high-salience date, and because Tehran publicly promised footage of him meeting commanders on August 26 that has still not appeared. The boring alternative is named and real: a wounded elderly cleric may simply be unwell, which produces identical observables and is why the forecast sits at 23% rather than in single digits. Falsifier: an independently authenticated live appearance in which he overrules a named IRGC position would break the model outright.

brief.h: Taiwan is back in the room in Palau, and a small island summit is the cheapest test of what Beijing's calm is actually for
brief.t: The Pacific Islands Forum leaders' meeting opened in Palau on Sunday and runs to September 4, with Taiwan attending after being excluded from last year's meeting in the Solomon Islands; foreign minister Lin Chia-lung is there for the Taiwan-Forum Countries Dialogue and a prosperity exhibit, Washington has publicly backed the presence, and Beijing has warned the Forum's secretary-general to adhere strictly to the one-China principle. Three of the eighteen members recognise Taipei rather than Beijing, and the host, Palau, is one of them. The Forum matters out of proportion to its size because this is where recognition is retail: a switch costs one small state's decision and buys permanent maritime, fisheries and diplomatic geometry. Read it as a gauge rather than a crisis - it tells you whether China's current softness on Taiwan is a pause bought for next month's summit or a ratchet that keeps turning through it.
brief.context: The rail here is old: the recognition contest runs on the 1971 settlement, when UN Resolution 2758 seated Beijing and left the question of Taiwan's representation to be fought state by state ever since, and the Pacific is the last liquid market in that trade. The desk that decides is not the PLA but the party's International Liaison Department and China's aid and fisheries bureaucracies, which is why the instrument this week is a warning letter to a secretary-general rather than a sortie - and why reading every Taiwan story through military signals gets the mechanism wrong. Follow the money: the recognition switches in Kiribati, the Solomon Islands and Nauru each tracked development finance and fisheries access, and what Taipei brings to Palau is the same currency at a smaller scale. The framework in play is our own tracked hypothesis, at 60%, that Beijing's detente is harvest cover - pressure that pauses for a summit is bargaining, pressure that persists through one is a ratchet - and the September 24 state visit is its resolution date, with coast guard presence east of Taiwan as the stated tell. Base rate discipline: gray-zone and diplomatic pressure campaigns very rarely convert into blockade, which is why the quarantine forecast held at 6% today even as the friction was loud. Falsifier for the harvest-cover read: Chinese coast guard presence east of Taiwan falling away through the visit rather than persisting.

brief.h: Guinea-Bissau's junta asked voters to ratify a stronger presidency - four months before the election meant to end junta rule
brief.t: Guinea-Bissau voted Sunday on a new constitution that would let the president appoint and dismiss the prime minister and cabinet, create and abolish ministries, chair the council of ministers and dissolve parliament in a grave political crisis, while cutting parliament from 102 seats to 65 and constituencies from 29 to 12. The military seized power in November 2025 after a disputed election in which both Umaro Sissoco Embalo and the opposition's Fernando Dias claimed victory; general elections are scheduled for December. Opposition parties urged a boycott and analysts question whether a government seated by coup has standing to rewrite a constitution at all. This is a standard sequence rather than an exception - seize, rewrite, then hold the vote inside the new rules - and it is worth watching precisely because nobody is watching.
brief.context: The mechanism deserves a name the reader can keep: constitutional laundering, in which an illegal seizure is converted into a legal order by referendum so that the election which follows can be technically free and structurally settled in advance. Follow the incentive rather than the rhetoric: a presidency that can dissolve parliament and dismiss the cabinet without legislative consent removes the one veto player a coup leader cannot otherwise buy, and compressing 29 constituencies into 12 concentrates the electoral map in ways that reward whoever controls national machinery. Base rate, and it is the load-bearing number: Guinea-Bissau has seen four successful coups and many more attempts since independence in 1974, and Powell and Thyne's coup dataset finds the single strongest predictor of a coup anywhere is a previous coup - the coup trap, in which each seizure teaches the officer corps that the method works. Regional context is a comparison set, not a cause: post-2020 juntas in Mali, Guinea, Burkina Faso and Niger each stretched or rewrote their transition timetables, while ECOWAS's leverage has collapsed since three members quit the bloc, so the external constraint that once priced this behaviour is largely gone. Falsifier for reading this as consolidation: a December election held on schedule, won by an opposition candidate who is allowed to take office. Watch the turnout figure first - a low-participation yes is a far weaker mandate than the headline result will be reported as.

lesson: Robert Pape's Bombing to Win examined every major strategic air campaign of the twentieth century and found a hard split. Punishment - hurting a population or an economy until the pain becomes unbearable - almost never produces political concessions, because states absorb suffering far better than planners assume and civilians cannot surrender on a government's behalf. Denial - destroying the enemy's physical ability to execute its military strategy - sometimes does work, because it changes what an army can actually do tomorrow rather than how a nation feels about it. Apply that to this weekend: Ukraine's drone campaign against Russian refineries is denial, since it starves the diesel that moves an army and the export earnings that fund it, and the evidence is Russian refinery runs at a 24-year low with most fuel exports banned to keep domestic pumps full. Russia's announced campaign against Ukraine's electricity grid is punishment - it will impose enormous civilian misery through a winter and has, on the historical record, a poor conversion rate into concessions at a negotiating table. The falsifiable prediction that follows: over the next six months expect Russia's fuel constraint to shape its behaviour more than Ukraine's blackouts shape Kyiv's, and if instead Ukraine's negotiating position visibly softens under grid attack while Russia's does not under fuel shortage, Pape's distinction is failing here and we should say so.

lecture.title: The Economic Weapon: Why Sieges Make the Wars They Mean to Prevent

sections.t: Treasury designated roughly sixty Chinese “teapot” refiners — the small plants buying discounted Iranian crude — while touching no Chinese state major and no bank. The same week, central banks bought a record 288.9 tonnes of gold in the quarter gold fell over 20%. Two stories, one machine.

sections.h: Follow the money, name the mechanism
sections.t: A reserve manager buying into a 20% drawdown is not trading. He is hedging ACCESS — the risk that an asset held abroad gets switched off by its host government — and gold is the only large reserve asset with no counterparty who can flip that switch. Name the mechanism: the ECONOMIC WEAPON, using the financial plumbing whose hubs one country owns to inflict a siege without laying one. Iran discounts crude to Chinese teapots paying through dollar-touching chains; Treasury designates them; the IRGC's Strait Authority recoups the shortfall in Hormuz tolls. Sanction and gold bar are one transaction seen from two ends.

sections.h: Deep history I — the blockade that became an idea
sections.t: The economic weapon has a birthday and a founding failure. The birthday is November 1806, when Napoleon's Berlin Decrees declared the British Isles blockaded — the Continental System, an attempt to beat a maritime power by closing a continent's markets to it. It succeeded at nothing except generating enforcement. Portugal would not comply, so France invaded in 1807 and got the Peninsular War, the ulcer that bled the Grande Armée for six years. Alexander I quit the system in December 1810 because it was ruining Russian trade, and in 1812 Napoleon marched east to enforce it. The blockade never defeated Britain; it manufactured the two wars that destroyed the blockader. Sanctions require enforcement, and enforcement against a determined leakage path tends toward conquest. The second case mattered because it worked. The Allied blockade of Germany ran from 1914 through the armistice and was lifted only when Germany signed at Versailles in June 1919. German official estimates put civilian deaths from malnutrition near 424,000 — contested, and historians still argue how much was blockade and how much German agricultural mismanagement. But perception makes policy, and a generation concluded hunger had beaten an undefeated army. So they institutionalized it as a PEACE instrument: Article 16 of the League Covenant made sanctions automatic against an aggressor, and Wilson in 1919 put it in words no Treasury official would dare use today — “A nation that is boycotted is a nation that is in sight of surrender. Apply this economic, peaceful, silent, deadly remedy and there will be no need for force.” The weapon was invented to ABOLISH war; the rest of the century refutes that sentence.

sections.h: Deep history II — the failures that define our problem
sections.t: ABYSSINIA, 1935. Italy invaded Ethiopia; the League invoked Article 16 — exempting oil, coal and steel, and never closing the Suez Canal, which Britain controlled and through which Italian troopships sailed. Mussolini won anyway. The sanctions were real enough to enrage and too porous to stop, and the lesson is sharper than “sanctions don't work”: a sanction calibrated to spare the sender teaches the target that the sender is deterred too. Then the second-order effect. Nicholas Mulder's argument in The Economic Weapon is that the interwar regime deterred small states and PROVOKED large ones. Italy, Germany and Japan drew the same conclusion from the 1930s — dependence on seaborne trade was a vulnerability an enemy could switch off at will, and the answer was autarky, self-sufficiency taken by force. Lebensraum and the Co-Prosperity Sphere were ideological projects; they were also sanctions-proofing programs. Japan is the proof case. Washington embargoed scrap iron in 1940, then froze Japanese assets on 26 July 1941; America supplied roughly 80% of Japan's oil, and with Britain and the Dutch East Indies following, Japan lost about 88% of its oil imports. Reserves would last three years at peace, half that at war — Nagano's image was of a patient wasting away, every month of compliance leaving Japan weaker against the enemy it expected to fight. Pearl Harbor came in December. And the detail that turns story into discipline: the freeze was never meant to be total. Roosevelt intended a licensing regime keeping oil flowing so the tap stayed usable as leverage; officials in State and Treasury administered it so strictly that no licences issued and the flow stopped. The sanction that helped produce Pearl Harbor was substantially an organizational outcome, not a presidential decision — Allison's Essence of Decision, live. Before inferring “Iran's strategy” from one action, ask which bureau took it.

sections.h: The pattern — and where it breaks
sections.t: The leakage path is always the whole story — not the designation list, the leak: Portugal and Russia in 1806, Beira and Pretoria in 1966, Chinese teapots now. NOW THE BREAK. Japan in 1941 had a military option that promised to SOLVE its resource problem: seize the Dutch East Indies and own the oil. Iran has none — it fought its war, lost the conventional exchange, and has played its asymmetric card, the Hormuz toll. Nor did 1914 face an alternative supplier: Iran's is the world's second-largest economy, which the sanctioner just spared. Less Pearl Harbor, more Rhodesia.

MULDER says the siege provokes: strangulation drives large states to autarky, then preemption. DREZNER says sanctions are cheap theater — Hufbauer's data give a third success rate at best, near zero against great powers. The 2026 evidence buries neither: it splits by SIDE, and the split is the finding. On the TARGET Mulder scores: gold, stockpiles, payment rails, enrichment acceleration under maximum pressure. On the SENDER Drezner scores harder — the carve-outs. Sixty teapots and not one bank is not escalation; it is the sanctioner taking its own threat hostage, because hitting a Chinese bank endangers the dollar system that makes the hammer heavy.

The 2015 architecture is not coming back (high confidence): the 2022 freeze of Russian reserves turned the settlement network into an instrument; a hedge once bought is not resold. Expect bifurcation, not de-dollarization (moderate-high). EICHENGREEN is right that currencies erode glacially; the WEAPON depreciates faster than the CURRENCY. The bolder call (moderate): the most dangerous decade is the one in which the weapon still works but no longer terrifies. Mulder's mechanism fires in the transition — invested in escaping, not finished, expecting strangulation regardless. For China, the 2030s — so Economic D-Day may SHORTEN the fuse it was meant to lengthen. FALSIFIER: designate a major Chinese state bank; if Beijing cuts Iranian purchases within a quarter, I am wrong. Two centuries say the economic weapon does not replace war — it sorts the world into blocs that survive each other's sieges, then gives the survivors a reason to fight.

Nicholas Mulder, The Economic Weapon (2022) — published weeks before the Russia sanctions matched its template. Farrell & Newman, “Weaponized Interdependence” (2019) — it called the 2022 playbook and the chip controls in advance. Eichengreen, Exorbitant Privilege — the counterweight.

events.label: Myla, Bucha district
events.note: A Russian strike on a munitions depot here killed 38 with four still missing - the deadliest single attack on Ukraine this year, and the second depot blast near Kyiv in under two months

events.label: Kirishi refinery
events.note: One of the northwestern plants in Kyiv's drone campaign that has cut Russian refinery runs to about 3.6m b/d, the lowest since May 2002

events.label: Pokrovsk
events.note: Still the axis Moscow names when it explains why it is in no hurry to talk; the Kremlin position remains a deep pause

events.label: Strait of Hormuz
events.note: Third straight day with no reported attack, but traffic is still roughly a tenth of the 130/day pre-war baseline and Tehran has not withdrawn a single condition

events.label: Kharg Island
events.note: Still idle under the US counter-blockade, roughly $170M a day of Iranian export revenue not moving

events.label: Muscat
events.note: Technical talks on a temporary corridor, joint mine clearance and the future administration of the strait; no coordinates and no minesweeping calendar published yet

events.label: Dubai
events.note: Treasury moved to cut Banque Misr's UAE branches off from US financial institutions over roughly $1.8bn processed for about 100 companies tied to Iran's shadow-banking network

events.label: Asheville, N.C.
events.note: Bessent hosts G20 finance ministers Monday and Tuesday, demanding members sever business ties with Iran while managing questions about US debt and yields

events.label: Bishkek
events.note: Putin, Xi and Modi convene for the SCO's 25th-anniversary summit on Sept 1 - the test of whether Moscow's deepening dependence on Beijing buys anything nameable

events.label: Koror, Palau
events.note: Taiwan seated at the Pacific Islands Forum over Beijing's objection and with US backing, after being excluded from last year's meeting

events.label: Bissau
events.note: A junta-run referendum on a constitution expanding presidential power, four months before the December election meant to end military rule

events.label: Nabatieh
events.note: Two months into the framework Israel says the Lebanese army has fallen short on dismantling Hezbollah infrastructure; still no agreed third-party verifier

fired: None today. Every named wire was checked against its threshold and none met it - logged deliberately so the non-fire is scoreable.

Hormuz: a third consecutive day with no reported attack at the strait, and nothing meeting the stricter wording either - no US-flagged or US-escorted vessel hit, no attack Iran publicly claimed, and no Israeli strike inside Iran during the corridor talks.
Ukraine: no Kremlin confirmation of a September round; the day's news ran the other way. China: no summit-cancellation signal, and Xi is confirmed for the SCO summit in Bishkek on Sept 1.

Near-wire, not fired: Russia's defence ministry publicly announced it is preparing massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. No Ukraine wire as written covers a THREATENED campaign, and a defence-ministry threat is cheap - so we are proposing the wire be respecified on outcome, not announcement.
armed: NEW - a single night's strike package causing rolling blackouts in three or more Ukrainian oblasts, or Ukrainian grid imports exceeding their 2025 winter peak (the energy-war wire, specified on damage rather than rhetoric)
Any attack on a US-flagged or US-escorted vessel - the sharpest open escalation trigger at the strait
A blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before Sept 24 - it would break the leverage-play read outright
A Kremlin confirmation of a September negotiating round - a reversal out of the deep pause
Ferry requisition, reserve mobilization or missile dispersal near Taiwan
Scholar-owned: IRGC/Basij defection (Takeyh) - casualty-recruitment crossover (Kofman) - PLA purge tempo (Fravel)

watch: Whether the announced Russian campaign against Ukraine's grid actually flies within six weeks, or stays a defence-ministry sentence - the falsifier on today's downgrade of the ceasefire forecast

Whether Moscow extends its diesel, gasoline and jet export ban past Oct 1 - each extension is a public admission of how much refining Kyiv's drones have taken offline, and it withdraws product from an already tight market

Whether the G20 communique in Asheville contains any collective language on Iran at all, or whether members quietly decline - the difference between a multilateral siege and a unilateral instrument others route around

Whether published Hormuz war-risk premia fall back under 3% of hull value - the London underwriting committee, not CENTCOM, sets the real reopening date, and the IMO has disputed the mine-free declaration

Whether any signed Venezuelan instrument appears with a stated term, settling the contradiction between Caracas saying 25 years and Washington describing a 100-year lease - paper, not adjectives, is the tell
